---
title: "Explore Florida household income by county"
execute:
  echo: false
---

Click a county on the map to see its median household income estimates from
2010 through 2023. The first chart shows Collier County.

```{r}
income <- readr::read_csv(
  "data/median_income.csv",
  col_types = readr::cols(GEOID = readr::col_character())
)
counties <- sf::st_read("data/florida_counties.geojson", quiet = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(GEOID = as.character(GEOID)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    income |> dplyr::filter(year == 2023) |> dplyr::select(GEOID, estimate),
    by = "GEOID"
  )

income_palette <- leaflet::colorNumeric("YlGnBu", domain = counties$estimate)

county_map <- leaflet::leaflet(counties, elementId = "county-map") |>
  leaflet::addProviderTiles(leaflet::providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>
  leaflet::addPolygons(
    layerId = ~GEOID,
    color = "#ffffff",
    weight = 1,
    fillColor = ~income_palette(estimate),
    fillOpacity = 0.8,
    label = ~paste0(NAME, ": $", scales::comma(estimate)),
    highlightOptions = leaflet::highlightOptions(
      weight = 2,
      color = "#263238",
      bringToFront = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  leaflet::addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    pal = income_palette,
    values = ~estimate,
    title = "2023 median income",
    labFormat = leaflet::labelFormat(prefix = "$")
  ) |>
  leaflet::fitBounds(-87.7, 24.3, -79.8, 31.1)

initial_county <- "12021"
initial_income <- income |> dplyr::filter(GEOID == initial_county)

htmlwidgets::onRender(
  county_map,
  sprintf(
    "function(el, x) {
      var income = %s;
      var map = this;
      var selectedLayer = null;

      function bindCounty(layer) {
        if (!layer.options || layer.options.layerId == null) return;

        if (String(layer.options.layerId) === '12021') {
          selectedLayer = layer;
          selectedLayer.setStyle({ weight: 3, color: '#263238' });
        }

        layer.on('click', function() {
          var geoid = String(layer.options.layerId);
          var countyRows = income.filter(function(row) {
            return row.GEOID === geoid;
          });
          if (!countyRows.length) return;

          if (selectedLayer) {
            selectedLayer.setStyle({ weight: 1, color: '#ffffff' });
          }
          selectedLayer = layer;
          selectedLayer.setStyle({ weight: 3, color: '#263238' });

          Plotly.react(
            document.querySelector('#income-chart .plotly'),
            [{
              x: countyRows.map(function(row) { return row.year; }),
              y: countyRows.map(function(row) { return row.estimate; }),
              type: 'scatter',
              mode: 'lines+markers',
              line: { color: '#28666e' },
              marker: { color: '#28666e' }
            }],
            {
              title: countyRows[0].county,
              xaxis: { title: 'ACS 5-year estimate ending year', dtick: 2 },
              yaxis: {
                title: 'Median household income',
                tickprefix: '$',
                tickformat: ',.0f'
              }
            },
            { responsive: true }
          );
        });
      }

      map.eachLayer(function(layer) {
        if (typeof layer.eachLayer === 'function') {
          layer.eachLayer(bindCounty);
        } else {
          bindCounty(layer);
        }
      });
    }",
    jsonlite::toJSON(
      income |> dplyr::select(GEOID, county, year, estimate),
      dataframe = "rows",
      auto_unbox = TRUE
    )
  )
)

htmltools::div(
  id = "income-chart",
  plotly::plot_ly(
    data = initial_income,
    x = ~year,
    y = ~estimate,
    type = "scatter",
    mode = "lines+markers",
    line = list(color = "#28666e"),
    marker = list(color = "#28666e")
  ) |>
    plotly::layout(
      title = "Collier County, Florida",
      xaxis = list(title = "ACS 5-year estimate ending year", dtick = 2),
      yaxis = list(
        title = "Median household income",
        tickprefix = "$",
        tickformat = ",.0f"
      )
    )
)
```

The map colors show 2023 estimates. Each point is an ACS 5-year estimate, so
neighboring points use overlapping years. Values are not adjusted for inflation.
The downloaded data also includes each estimate's margin of error.
